SMTO-CFG-0044 — SMTO's command output limit must be above zero

GUID: d6421c28-4a6d-4215-a3e5-989eed8834d7
Slug: config-runtime-shell-max-output-chars-must-be
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting limits how much of each command's output SMTO keeps for the agent to read, but it is set to zero or less, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find shell_max_output_chars under the runtime section. That line sets how many characters of each command's output SMTO keeps.
  2. Change it to a positive number, or delete the line to use the standard 20,000 characters. Then start SMTO again. With a limit of zero or less, SMTO couldn't keep any command output at all.
  3. If SMTO still stops with this message, make sure you edited the file SMTO really uses: the one given after --config when it was started, or config.yaml in SMTO's own folder. SMTO may be reading a different copy of the settings file than the one you changed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits or timeouts to work around this; only the output limit is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration validation failed because runtime.shell_max_output_chars in the application YAML is zero or negative.

What this means

  • The structured runtime section sets shell_max_output_chars at or below zero. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The structured runtime section sets shell_max_output_chars at or below zero.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect runtime.shell_max_output_chars separately from model response/context budgets.

How to fix it

  • Set runtime.shell_max_output_chars in the bootstrap YAML to a positive integer, or omit it for the 20000-character default; it bounds the shell output preview passed to the execution engine. AOR_SHELL_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS overrides the effective value later; a nonpositive environment value is rejected by Settings and reported as SMTO-CFG-0060, not this error.
  • Set runtime.shell_max_output_chars to a supported positive character count.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The runtime accepts the intended positive shell output character bound.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
